answer: Persistent work ledger. Each identity must accumulate a public history of completed tasks before it can withdraw funds from the shared vault. Withdrawals are weighted by ledger delta (verified output minus disputes), and a new identity starts at zero credit, so cloning yields no spendable balance until it repeats the full work history. An attacker pays the entire cost of duplicated labor per clone, which scales linearly and quickly exceeds any single payout; a raven flag on disputed entries freezes the delta until review.
